text:
Ava: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands — using this thread for detailed questions about release rituals, oncall shifts, quality bars, and SLAs. I'll answer or tag owners. Please keep Qs short and we'll thread answers. Starting: what's the runway for changing our release freeze policy?
Diego: For the release freeze, proposal is to relax minor-patch freeze from 48h -> 24h, keep 72h for major releases. We think this lowers friction for urgent fixes. @Liam can confirm SRE impact.
Liam: SRE perspective: 24h for patch-only releases OK if CI + canary pass. Need automation: canary gate should verify canary_error_rate < 1% and latency regressions <5%. We'll add an alert rule and a dashboard panel.
Priya: How will this affect Dedicated customers / maintenance windows? Do we need contractual notice before a patch that may affect latency? @Product or Legal — ping.
Maya: On the "quality bars" note — can we have a short checklist for "ship-ready"? e.g., critical-path unit tests, integration smoke, changelog, perf guardrail. Not a hard coverage number.
Ava: Agreed — we'll publish a concise ship checklist. Coverage percentage shouldn't be the blocker; focus on critical path tests + smoke + perf checks. I'll draft and share in #eng-process tomorrow.
Nora: About oncall rotations — current policy requires 2-week notice for swaps. Can we add a one-time swap with your oncall buddy for last-minute conflicts?
Liam: Operationally we can permit single swaps with sign-off from the rotation lead and an update to PagerDuty schedule. Requirement: swapping must not reduce overlap for handoffs. Please file as a calendar invite + PD change.
Diego: SLA question: Hosted API 99.9% — how are we measuring failures? Are client retries counted?
Ava: SLA measures server-side failures (5xx + gateway errors). Client-side retries don't change SLA for the customer; we count requests accepted by our gateway. We'll clarify examples in the SLA doc.
SamBot: deploy-bot: "Canary rollout policy: default 30% traffic for 15m, auto-promote on green metrics. See /deploy canary-policy for config."
Maya: Practical: for hotfixes please include a changelog entry even if tiny — it saves support triage.
Diego: +1 :thumbsup: Also can we get a small template for post-deploy checks? e.g., CPU, mem, 99p latency, error rate.
Priya: I'll create templates for maintenance notices and a post-deploy checklist and link them in #eng-process by EOD Friday.
Liam: Example canary check command we use in SRE runbooks:
```
curl -sS https://metrics.internal/api/query -d 'metric=canary_error_rate&window=15m' | jq '.value < 0.01'
```
Maya: Another tiny ask — add a line to the ship checklist reminding folks to run the perf smoke for the top-3 customer flows.
Ava: Thanks everyone. If you have concrete examples (configs, past incidents, checklist snippets), drop them here and we'll fold them into the doc. I'll summarize and close the thread next week. :white_check_mark:
